AppImage runtime: libfuse source and relinking information

The Linux AppImage runtime uses a statically linked libfuse 3.15.0 library,
including the upstream AppImage mount.c patch. The library and its use are
covered by LGPL-2.1; the accompanying LICENSE and LGPL2.txt explain its terms.
Other components retain their own licenses. Visual Agent does not prohibit
modification for your own use or reverse engineering to debug such changes.

This source-and-relink route requires visual-agent-corresponding-sources.zip
to accompany the AppImage download. An incomplete development candidate without
that matching archive has not completed this route. Extract the archive; its
source-materials/archives/appimage-runtime directory includes:

- fuse-3.15.0.tar.xz: original complete libfuse source;
- type2-runtime-dd6cebed.tar.gz: AppImage runtime source, build scripts,
  and patches/libfuse/mount.c.diff;
- source archives and package recipes for the other retained runtime inputs.

The original libfuse archive SHA-256 is:
70589cfd5e1cff7ccd6ac91c86c01be340b227285c5e200baa284e401eea2ca0

The runtime source archive SHA-256 is:
f5fec23be76e50e2445ed2d018bac49b367490fc483c62c4637e99ec705d27ba

Rebuild/relink on Linux:

1. Extract the runtime source archive and read its BUILD.md. Use the supplied
   Docker method, not the chroot method on an ordinary host. The build requires
   Docker, disk space for its image, and network access for build dependencies.
2. The dependency installer verifies the original libfuse archive, then applies
   patches/libfuse/mount.c.diff and builds the library. To change the library,
   extend that patch with your source changes while retaining the upstream
   patch and applicable license/modification notices. Do not present changed
   source archives as having the original checksum.
3. From the extracted runtime source directory, run:
   ARCH=x86_64 bash scripts/docker/build-with-docker.sh
   The Docker build copies the patch directory, so changing the patch rebuilds
   libfuse before the runtime is linked. The output is runtime-x86_64.
4. To use your runtime with the application, extract an AppImage using its
   --appimage-extract option, then use appimagetool's --runtime-file option
   with your rebuilt runtime and the extracted squashfs-root AppDir. Create a
   new output AppImage; do not overwrite the original while testing it.

This is a source-and-relink route under LGPL-2.1 section 6(a), not a promise of
byte-identical reproduction of an upstream binary. Build-tool availability and
Alpine repository contents can change. Preserve the source and notices supplied
with the release; use the recorded sources and recipes when investigating
dependency changes. This guide does not grant release clearance or replace the
licenses of the runtime and its constituent libraries.
